candidates.old:
.check_for_collision_with_mover
    JSR get_mover_X_type_and_height
    STA &78
    LDA mover_types_width_table,Y
    STA &7A
    CLC                             \ grind: the right edge first (x + width >= mover_x, 16-bit), the test more movers fail
    ADC movers_x_low,X
    TAY
    LDA movers_x_high,X
    ADC #0                          \ (x + width) high, wrapping as the original's INY did
    CPY mover_x_low
    SBC &C5
    BCC leave_with_carry_as_is      \ C=0: no collision
    LDA mover_x_max_low             \ then x <= mover_x_max (16-bit)
    CMP movers_x_low,X
    LDA mover_x_max_high
    SBC movers_x_high,X
    BCC leave_with_carry_as_is      \ C=0: no collision
    LDA movers_y,X
    CMP mover_y_max
    BCS leave_with_carry_clear_28c9
    ADC &78
    CMP mover_y                     \ grind: C=0 (no collision) or C=1 (collision) is the answer
candidates.new:
.check_for_collision_with_mover
    LDA mover_x_max_low             \ grind: x <= mover_x_max (16-bit) first: it needs no type or width, and
    CMP movers_x_low,X              \ fails 5,213 of the 13,260 checks a 1,000 passes (seed 1, passes 500-1500), the
    LDA mover_x_max_high            \ right edge below only 6,404 and at four times the cost
    SBC movers_x_high,X
    BCC leave_with_carry_as_is      \ C=0: no collision
    LDA movers_type_and_colour,X    \ then the right edge (x + width >= mover_x, 16-bit): the type looked up here,
    AND #&7F                        \ the height only if the y test is reached (get_mover_X_type_and_height inlined
    TAY                             \ down to its type; STA &78 and STA &7A were dead: nothing reads them after)
    LDA mover_types_width_table,Y
    CLC
    ADC movers_x_low,X
    TAY
    LDA movers_x_high,X
    ADC #0                          \ (x + width) high, wrapping as the original's INY did
    CPY mover_x_low
    SBC &C5
    BCC leave_with_carry_as_is      \ C=0: no collision
    LDA movers_y,X
    CMP mover_y_max
    BCS leave_with_carry_clear_28c9
    JSR get_mover_X_type_and_height \ A = height (Y = type): only for the checks that get this far
    CLC
    ADC movers_y,X
    CMP mover_y                     \ grind: C=0 (no collision) or C=1 (collision) is the answer
candidates.summary: check_for_collision_with_mover: test x <= mover_x_max first (no type lookup), then the right edge with the type looked up inline, and the height (get_mover_X_type_and_height, now only for checks that pass both x tests and the y-max test) last; the dead STA &78 / STA &7A go. Measured (unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, seed 1, passes 500-1500, per 1,000 passes): 13,260 entries, the x_max test fails 5,213, the right edge fails 6,000 of the other 8,047, 2,047 reach the y test, 1,954 the height. Alternative to candidates 2 and 3 (same lines).
candidates.equivalence: The result is C = (x_max >= x) AND (x + width >= mover_x, 16-bit as before) AND (y < y_max) AND (y + height >= mover_y), each exit leaving C=0 for a failed test as before; the tests have no side effects so their order does not change the result. The y test's A = y + height (8-bit, as ADC &78 with C=0 gave) is now CLC : ADC movers_y,X on the JSR's height A. X is never changed. Callers (check_in_full, friends_in_full, search_in_full, check_for_player_collision_with_mover_Y's BEQ, check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X's fall-through) read only C and X after the return and reload A and Y (check_if_friendly, check_for_hostile_collision, not_hostile, kill_mover's LDY &87, etc.); &78/&7A are written before every read in all their other uses (y_velocity, right_high, y_offset, colour, initial_new_movers_offset, row_screen_address_low: game.6502 and bank5 grep). check_if_mover_is_on_edge, the only &7A reader that does not write first, has no caller. No entry past the label (grep 'check_for_collision_with_mover *+' finds none). A, Y, &78, &7A on exit differ from before (dead).
candidates.relies_on: No caller reads A, Y, &78 or &7A after the return (see equivalence); get_mover_X_type_and_height preserves X and is a plain JSR target. Page crossings: the code is 56 bytes (was 52) in the page of &254B (unshifted builds) so every branch in it stays in-page (BCC leave_with_carry_as_is forward ~35-50 bytes); everything after it in main RAM slides 4 bytes up to the next SKIP (unused_3400_original, 193 free): hot branches and indexed reads after &2580 may cross a page differently - the gate measures it, candidate 3 is the 0-byte alternative.
